h1: Criminal Record Expungement (Expunction) in El Paso, Texas
intro: A dismissed case still shows up on a background check until a court orders it erased. Attorney Robert Navar files expunction petitions in El Paso County district court so the arrest, the charge and the booking record are destroyed — not just hidden.
summary: An expunction under Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 55A (formerly Chapter 55) orders every agency that holds a record of your arrest or charge to destroy it, and lets you lawfully deny the arrest ever happened.

You generally qualify if the case was dismissed, you were acquitted, a grand jury no-billed it, or you completed deferred disposition on a Class C misdemeanor. Some arrests that never led to a charge qualify after a waiting period.
The petition is filed in El Paso County district court at 500 E. San Antonio Ave; most uncontested expunctions take a few months from filing to a signed order.
We confirm eligibility against the current statute before filing and quote a flat fee after a free consultation. Call 915-503-1600 or schedule an appointment.

sections.heading: What an Expunction Actually Does to Your Record
paragraphs: People use "expunge" and "seal" as if they were the same thing. In Texas they are not. An order of expunction under Chapter 55A directs every agency named in the order — police, sheriff, DPS, the prosecutor, the court clerk — to return or destroy the records of the arrest and charge. Once the order is final, you can legally say you were never arrested for that offense, including on job applications and most government forms. The only common exception is a later criminal proceeding where the expunged matter itself is at issue.

An order of nondisclosure, by contrast, seals the record from the public and from private background-check companies but leaves it visible to law enforcement, licensing boards and certain state agencies. Expunction is the stronger remedy, and it is the one most of our former ticket clients actually qualify for, because Class C misdemeanors that ended in dismissal are expungeable.

Expunction does not reach everything. A case that ended in a conviction is generally not expungeable, and a record that was already sealed by nondisclosure does not automatically become expungeable later. We check both paths against your actual court history before recommending one.

sections.heading: Who Qualifies for Expunction in Texas
paragraphs: Chapter 55A lists the situations in which a person is entitled to an expunction. The ones we see most often in El Paso are below. Eligibility rules change — the chapter was recodified in 2025 — so we confirm your facts against the current statute before anything is filed.

list.text: the charge was dismissed and the indictment or information, if any, was quashed or dismissed because it was based on mistake, false information or a similar reason, or the limitations period has run.
you went to trial and were found not guilty, or were convicted and later pardoned or found actually innocent.
the grand jury declined to indict and the waiting period has passed.
the ticket or other Class C charge was dismissed after you finished deferred disposition under art. 45.051. These are generally eligible once the deferral is completed.
an arrest that never produced a charge may be expunged after a waiting period that depends on the offense level, or sooner if the prosecutor certifies the records are no longer needed.

sections.heading: How the El Paso Expunction Process Works
paragraphs: We start by pulling the real record: your DPS criminal history, the court's disposition, and in Class C cases the El Paso Municipal Court or Justice of the Peace file showing the deferred disposition and dismissal. Clients are often surprised to learn a "dismissed" ticket was actually paid as a conviction, or that a warrant arrest years ago created a booking record they never knew about. That review is free.

If you qualify, we draft a verified petition for expunction and file it in an El Paso County district court. The petition must name every agency that may hold a record: the El Paso Police Department, the El Paso County Sheriff's Office, Texas DPS, the District or County Attorney, the City Attorney for municipal cases, the court clerk and any jail or magistrate that processed you. Missing an agency means that agency keeps the record, so this list is where experience matters.

The court sets a hearing at least 30 days out so the agencies can respond. For an eligible, well-documented petition, the hearing is usually brief or waived and the judge signs the order. The clerk then sends certified copies to each agency, which must destroy the records and confirm. Start to finish, a typical uncontested El Paso expunction runs a few months.

sections.heading: Why Expunction Matters More in El Paso
paragraphs: El Paso's job market runs on background checks. Fort Bliss contractors, federal positions, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the ports of entry, hospitals, school districts and the trucking companies along I-10 all screen applicants, and many of those screens pull directly from the DPS database and from court records. A ten-year-old driving while license invalid arrest or a dismissed Class C charge can show up as an "arrest record" with no disposition, which an HR reviewer reads as unresolved.

Security clearances and federal applications ask about arrests, not just convictions. Without an expunction, you have to disclose the arrest and explain it. With one, the honest answer is no. For clients applying to CBP, Border Patrol, the military or a licensed profession, that difference decides whether the application moves forward.

Private background-check vendors also scrape court data and keep stale copies. An expunction order gives you the legal basis to force them to remove the record, and we provide the certified copy you need to do it.

sections.heading: Cost and Timing of an El Paso Expunction
paragraphs: We handle expunctions on a flat fee quoted after a free consultation, because the work depends on how many arrests, courts and agencies are involved. A single Class C case dismissed after deferred disposition is the simplest; a petition covering several arrests across municipal, JP and county courts takes more drafting and more service. Court filing fees and certified-copy charges are separate and we tell you the total up front. Former ticket clients of the firm get priority scheduling — see our deferred adjudication record cleanup page.

Timing depends on the court's docket and how quickly agencies respond, but most eligible petitions are signed within a few months of filing. If a job application or clearance deadline is driving the timeline, tell us at the consultation and we will plan around it. faqs.q: What is the difference between expunction and nondisclosure in Texas?
faqs.a: Expunction orders the records destroyed and lets you deny the arrest; it is available mainly for dismissals, acquittals, no-bills and completed Class C deferrals. Nondisclosure seals the record from the public but keeps it visible to law enforcement and licensing agencies; it is the remedy for most completed deferred adjudications and certain convictions.

faqs.q: Can a traffic ticket be expunged in El Paso?
faqs.a: Generally yes, if the ticket was dismissed — including a dismissal after deferred disposition. A ticket you simply paid is a conviction and is not expungeable. We check the court's disposition first, because many people remember the outcome differently than the clerk recorded it.

faqs.q: How long does an expunction take in El Paso County?
faqs.a: Most uncontested petitions are signed within a few months of filing. The court must give agencies at least 30 days' notice before the hearing, and after the order is signed the clerk mails certified copies to each agency for destruction of the records.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court for the expunction hearing?
faqs.a: Usually not. For an eligible, unopposed petition the hearing is brief and we appear for you. If an agency objects or the judge wants testimony, we will prepare you and attend together.

faqs.q: Is there a waiting period before I can file?
faqs.a: It depends on how the case ended. Dismissals after completed Class C deferred disposition are generally eligible once the deferral is done. Arrests that never resulted in a charge may require a waiting period based on the offense level. We confirm the applicable period under the current statute before filing.

faqs.q: What does an El Paso expunction cost?
faqs.a: We quote a flat fee after a free consultation, based on the number of arrests, courts and agencies involved. Filing fees and certified copies are additional and disclosed up front. Call 915-503-1600 or book a consultation online.
